title: Ephemeral Servers
description: Short-lived servers across providers that push their own metrics via remote_write. Fully separated from the fixed infrastructure.

list.name: node
list.label: Server
list.description: Only servers currently pushing. Uses query_result rather than label_values: label_values reads the index, and the index still holds the names of series that were deleted until the block is compacted. query_result runs a real query.

panels.title: Ephemeral servers up
panels.description: If this is 0, no ephemeral servers are running — which is the normal state, not a problem.

panels.title: Age — forgotten?
panels.description:
The most important panel here. The problem with ephemeral servers is not that they die, it is that they are forgotten and keep billing.

Green under 24h, orange over 24h, red over 72h.

Shows only servers that are CURRENTLY pushing. The `and on(server) (up == 1)` filter is needed because the "All" option on the $node variable becomes ".*", which also matches servers that have already been shut down.

panels.title: Total in (netIn)
panels.description:
Bytes that actually flowed during the SELECTED TIME RANGE in the top right — change the range and this number changes with it.

Uses increase() rather than a plain difference, because node_network_*_bytes_total is a counter that resets to zero on every reboot or interface reset. increase() recognises the reset instead of reading it as a huge negative spike.

lo and docker0 are excluded: the first is traffic to itself, the second is inter-container traffic that never leaves the machine.

Shows only servers that are CURRENTLY pushing. The `and on(server) (up == 1)` filter is needed because the "All" option on the $node variable becomes ".*", which also matches servers that have already been shut down.

targets.expr: sum by (server, city, provider) (increase(node_network_receive_bytes_total{job="node-ephemeral",server=~"$node",device!~"lo|docker.*|veth.*|br-.*|podman.*|cni.*|tun.*"}[$__range])) and on(server) (up{job="node-ephemeral"} == 1)

lo and docker0 are excluded: the first is traffic to itself, the second is inter-container traffic that never leaves the machine.

targets.expr: sum by (server, city, provider) (increase(node_network_transmit_bytes_total{job="node-ephemeral",server=~"$node",device!~"lo|docker.*|veth.*|br-.*|podman.*|cni.*|tun.*"}[$__range])) and on(server) (up{job="node-ephemeral"} == 1)

panels.title: CPU used (%)
panels.description:
rate() gives the per-second increase of the idle CPU counter; subtracting from 100 yields percent used.

Note `avg without(cpu, mode)` rather than `avg by(instance)`. Both average across cores, but by(instance) DROPS every other label, leaving the {{city}} legend empty. without() removes only the two labels named and keeps the rest.

Shows only servers that are CURRENTLY pushing. The `and on(server) (up == 1)` filter is needed because the "All" option on the $node variable becomes ".*", which also matches servers that have already been shut down.

panels.title: Memory used (%)
panels.description:
See the "Memory now" panel for why this uses MemAvailable.

Shows only servers that are CURRENTLY pushing. The `and on(server) (up == 1)` filter is needed because the "All" option on the $node variable becomes ".*", which also matches servers that have already been shut down.

panels.title: Network throughput
panels.description:
Instantaneous rate, not a total. Outbound is drawn negative so both directions are readable in one graph without hiding each other.

Multiplied by 8 to convert bytes/s into bits/s — the unit providers quote for link capacity.

Shows only servers that are CURRENTLY pushing. The `and on(server) (up == 1)` filter is needed because the "All" option on the $node variable becomes ".*", which also matches servers that have already been shut down.

targets.expr: sum by (server, city, provider) (rate(node_network_receive_bytes_total{job="node-ephemeral",server=~"$node",device!~"lo|docker.*|veth.*|br-.*|podman.*|cni.*|tun.*"}[5m])) * 8 and on(server) (up{job="node-ephemeral"} == 1)

panels.title: Volume per 5 minutes
panels.description:
How many bytes flowed WITHIN each 5-minute window — not a rate, not cumulative. Each bar stands alone.

Difference from "Network throughput" above: throughput answers "how fast right now" (bits/s), this answers "how much during that period" (bytes). For estimating transfer quota usage, this is the relevant one.

For the buckets to neither overlap nor leave gaps, the range inside increase() must match the query step. Hence Min interval = 5m and Max data points = 3000 — enough to span a full 7 days without forcing Grafana to widen the step.

Outbound is drawn negative.

Shows only servers that are CURRENTLY pushing. The `and on(server) (up == 1)` filter is needed because the "All" option on the $node variable becomes ".*", which also matches servers that have already been shut down.

targets.expr: sum by (server, city, provider) (increase(node_network_receive_bytes_total{job="node-ephemeral",server=~"$node",device!~"lo|docker.*|veth.*|br-.*|podman.*|cni.*|tun.*"}[5m])) and on(server) (up{job="node-ephemeral"} == 1)

panels.title: Push pipeline health
panels.description:
The ONLY panel here not filtered to active servers — deliberately. This is exactly where you want to see a server that STOPPED: the broken line marks when it quit pushing.

The `up` metric here is not generated by the hub. The hub pulls nothing from ephemeral servers, it only receives. This value is produced by the agent on the server itself and pushed along with everything else.

panels.title: Ephemeral server inventory
panels.description:
Labels are carried by the agent on the server itself at bootstrap, not written into the hub's config. A new server appears here without the hub being touched.

Shows only servers that are CURRENTLY pushing. The `and on(server) (up == 1)` filter is needed because the "All" option on the $node variable becomes ".*", which also matches servers that have already been shut down.
